title: How to make a chart in Numbers on Mac: step by step for Numbers 15.4

description: Learn how to make a chart in Numbers on Mac in four steps: select cells, click the Chart button, pick a style, and fix the data.

intro: To make a chart in Numbers on Mac, select the table cells you want to plot, then click the Chart button in the toolbar. Choose 2D, 3D, or Interactive, click a style, and the chart appears on your sheet.
tldr: Select the table cells you want to plot. Include a header row or column so the chart gets labels.
Click the Chart button in the toolbar, then choose 2D, 3D, or Interactive.
Click a style to insert it, or drag it onto the sheet where you want it.
If the chart stays empty or skips data, check for text in number cells, hidden rows, and summary rows.

blocks.text: Numbers comes free with new Macs, so you may already have it. Apple describes the chart tool as the Chart button in the toolbar, not as an Insert menu item. Look for the chart control in the toolbar first. Everything below follows Apple's workflow for Numbers 15.4, the version its Mac guide covers.
Check which version of Numbers you have first

Click Numbers in the menu bar, then click About Numbers. The window shows your version. Apple's guide covers Numbers 15.4. The App Store listing shows 15.4.2, dated Oct 23. Both require macOS 26 or later, according to Apple and the App Store.

Older copies may look different. Numbers 15.1 launched January 28, 2026 as a rewritten app, not an in-place update. It installs next to Numbers 14.5, which no longer receives updates. TidBITS says 15.1 needs macOS 15.6 Sequoia, which does not match the macOS 26 requirement from Apple. Check your macOS version before you assume an update is possible.

items: Numbers 15.4 or later: follow the steps in this guide as written.
Numbers 14.5: it no longer gets updates, so menus may not match these steps.
macOS older than 26: Apple lists macOS 26 or later for Numbers 15.4, so update macOS before you expect these menus.

blocks.text: Step by step: make a chart from existing cells
The steps below cover the most common job. You have a table with labels in one row or column and numbers beside them. Keep the sheet open next to this page, and work through each step in order.
Add the chart first, then choose its data

Sometimes you want the chart on the sheet before you choose its data. Apple's guide covers that route too. The chart sits on the sheet, and you fill in its data afterward. This works well when you are still deciding which numbers matter.

items: Add a chart to the sheet and make sure it is selected.
Click Add Chart Data, which appears near the selected chart.
Select the table cells you want to plot.
Click Done in the bottom bar.

blocks.text: The pop-up in the bottom bar sets rows or columns as series. Check it before you click Done. It decides how Numbers groups your numbers, and a wrong choice gives you a chart that reads backward.
Choose rows or columns as series in Numbers

A series is one group of values, such as one product tracked over time. It gets its own color or line in the chart. If your months run down a column and each product has its own column, you usually want one series per product. If the chart runs the other way, change the orientation instead of rebuilding the table.

items: Click the chart to select it.
Click Edit Data References.
Use the pop-up in the bottom bar to set rows or columns as series.
Click Done.

blocks.text: Read the legend before and after you change the orientation. The legend names each series. If the names match what you expect, the chart is right. If they do not, change the pop-up again.
Make an interactive chart in Numbers on Mac

An interactive chart lets readers switch what they see with on-screen controls. Use it for a file people will explore. Keep a static 2D chart for a printed report or a slide that does not need controls.

items: Click the Chart button in the toolbar, then click Interactive.
Click a chart or drag it onto the sheet.
Click Add Chart Data, select the cells, then click Done.
To change the control type, open the Format sidebar, click the Chart tab, and use the pop-up below Interactive Chart. Buttons Only is one option.

blocks.text: If the Format sidebar is hidden, press Option-Command-I to show or hide it. Apple lists that shortcut in its keyboard list for Numbers on Mac.
Pick 2D or 3D, and know what carries over
Use 2D for most work. A 2D column or bar chart makes exact values easier to read than a 3D version. Pick 3D only when the chart is for a presentation, and the shape matters more than precise reading.

3D charts behave differently across apps. Numbers for iCloud shows imported 3D charts as 2D, but keeps the 3D data. The chart returns to 3D when the file opens in Numbers on Mac, iPhone, or iPad. Plan for that if you share the file in a browser.
Fix a chart that is blank, short, or plotted wrong

Most broken charts come from four causes: text in number cells, hidden rows, grouped tables, and large data sets. Check them in that order. Start with the data, because a styling change will not fix missing numbers.

Text causes most empty charts. An older Apple Community thread from the Numbers 3 era describes a chart that stayed blank because only the text column was selected. The fix in that thread was a summary table with names in a header column and numeric totals beside them. That thread predates the current app, so treat it as a clue, not a guarantee.

Hidden data stays out of the chart by default. Hidden or filtered rows are excluded. To include them, click the chart, open the Format sidebar, click the Chart tab, and select Hidden Data in Chart Options. If you filter the table on purpose, read [how to filter a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/filter-table-rows-in-numbers) first.

Grouped tables cause a quieter problem. In a categorized table, the first selected cell must not be in a summary row if you want individual data points. If your selection includes a collapsed group, only data from visible groups is plotted. Expand the groups, then select the cells again.

Large data sets get a sample. For large column, bar, line, or area charts, Numbers shows a representative sample of each series. Your table data does not change. To see the message, click Large Data Set in the Format sidebar Chart tab.
Mistakes people make when charting in Numbers

items: Selecting only the numbers and leaving out the labels. The legend and axis then show generic names.
Leaving a value as text. It looks right in the cell but stays empty in the chart.
Forgetting that a hidden or filtered row is not charted.
Selecting a summary row by accident, which changes what gets plotted.
Picking 3D for a comparison chart, then reading bar heights by eye.
Expecting a 3D chart to stay 3D in Numbers for iCloud. It shows flat there.

blocks.text: Fix these before you style the chart. Colors and fonts do not help a chart that plots the wrong rows.
Edit, move, and export your chart
Click a chart and drag it to move it. Drag it away from the table if the two overlap, so you can see both while you work.
If you insert the wrong style, press Command-Z to undo. Press Shift-Command-Z to redo. Apple lists both shortcuts in its keyboard list for Numbers on Mac.

To put the chart in a report, export the sheet. The steps are in [how to export Numbers to PDF on Mac](/how-to/export-a-spreadsheet-to-pdf-in-numbers). To send the file to someone, [share a spreadsheet in Numbers](/how-to/share-a-spreadsheet-in-numbers) covers invites and links.
Numbers for iCloud: the web chart steps

The web version follows a similar path. Select your data, click the Chart button in the toolbar, click 2D or Interactive, then choose a type. Apple's iCloud guide says only column, bar, scatter, and bubble charts can be interactive on the web.
If your file moves between Numbers on Mac and iCloud, check the chart type after each trip. The 3D note above applies here too.
Is Numbers free for making charts?
Numbers is free with new Macs, iPhones, and iPads. Apple's Creator Studio page says that without a subscription you keep access to these apps but lose the intelligence features.

Creator Studio costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year, according to the App Store listing. It adds premium content and intelligence features. Apple's chart pages do not list a subscription as a requirement. If an app prompts you to pay while you chart, check the App Store listing first.
Where to go after your first chart
Build the source table first if you do not have one. [How to add a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/add-a-table-in-numbers) covers the Table button and styles.

Add totals with a formula when the chart needs them. [How to add a formula in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/add-a-formula-to-a-cell-in-numbers) covers the steps. If a total sits in a summary row, read the grouped-table warning above before you select it.
Filter the table before you chart a subset. Hidden rows stay out of the chart by default, so filter first, then check the chart again.

faq.question: How do I make a chart in Numbers on Mac without selecting data first?
faq.answer: Add the chart to the sheet and make sure it is selected. Click Add Chart Data near it, select your table cells, and click Done in the bottom bar. The chart fills in after you choose the cells.

faq.question: Where is the chart button in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: It sits in the toolbar at the top of the window. Apple's guide describes it as the Chart button. Apple's keyboard shortcut list has no shortcut for inserting a chart, so use the toolbar.

faq.question: Why is my chart empty in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Check that your values are numbers, not text. Then check hidden rows, summary rows, and collapsed groups. The Apple Community thread on this problem dates from the Numbers 3 era, so the menus may differ today.

faq.question: Can I switch rows and columns after the chart is made?
faq.answer: Yes. Click the chart, click Edit Data References, and use the pop-up in the bottom bar to set rows or columns as series. The shortcut is Shift-Command-D. Click Done when the chart looks right.

faq.question: What is the difference between 2D and interactive charts in Numbers?
faq.answer: A 2D chart is static. An interactive chart adds on-screen controls so readers can switch what they see. Apple's guide lists Interactive as an option under the Chart button.

faq.question: Does Numbers for iCloud support 3D charts?
faq.answer: It shows imported 3D charts as 2D, but it keeps the 3D data. The 3D view returns when you open the file in Numbers on Mac, iPhone, or iPad.

faq.question: Do I need Creator Studio to make charts in Numbers?
faq.answer: Numbers is free with new Macs. Creator Studio costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year and adds premium content and intelligence features. Apple's chart pages do not list it as a requirement.

faq.question: Which version of Numbers should I use for these steps?
faq.answer: Use the latest Numbers 15.x that your macOS supports. Apple's guide covers Numbers 15.4, and the App Store lists 15.4.2. Click Numbers in the menu bar, then About Numbers, to check yours.

task: Make a chart in Numbers on Mac
appliesTo: Numbers for Mac 15.4 on macOS 26 or later
requirements: A Mac running macOS 26 or later, per Apple's requirement for Numbers 15.4
Numbers for Mac 15.4 or later, free with new Macs
A table with labels in one row or column and numeric values beside them

steps.name: Open the sheet with your data
steps.text: Open your Numbers file and go to the sheet that holds the table. Check that the values you want to chart are real numbers. A value that looks like a number but is stored as text leaves the chart empty.
steps.tip: Keep one header row at the top, so the chart can label each series.

steps.name: Select the cells you want to plot
steps.text: Drag across the cells you want. Include a header row or header column if you want labels. To select a whole row or column, click its row number or column letter. Cells can come from more than one table, even on different sheets.
steps.tip: Select labels with the numbers. Otherwise the chart may show generic names.

steps.name: Click the Chart button in the toolbar
steps.text: Look at the toolbar at the top of the window and click the Chart button. Apple's Mac guide describes it this way. The chart options open with 2D, 3D, and Interactive choices.
steps.tip: Apple's guide does not describe an Insert menu item for charts, so look in the toolbar.

steps.name: Choose 2D, 3D, or Interactive
steps.text: Pick 2D for most reports, because it keeps values easy to compare. Pick 3D only when the look matters more than precise reading. Use the arrows to see more styles in the family you chose.
steps.tip: Interactive charts add controls that readers can use. Save them for files people explore.

steps.name: Click a style to insert it
steps.text: Click the chart you want, and Numbers inserts it with your selected cells as its data. You can also drag a chart onto the sheet to put it exactly where you want. Apple's guide describes both options.
steps.tip: Drag a chart away from the table first, so the two do not overlap.

steps.name: Check the chart against your table
steps.text: Read the title, the labels, and the series. Make sure each bar or line matches the row or column you meant. If the grouping looks wrong, change the series orientation rather than rebuilding the chart.
steps.tip: Compare one value on the chart with the same value in the table.

steps.name: Change the series orientation if needed
steps.text: Click the chart, then click Edit Data References. Use the pop-up in the bottom bar to set rows or columns as series. Click Done when the chart looks right.
steps.tip: Shift-Command-D is the shortcut for Edit Data References in Apple's list.

steps.name: Undo a chart you do not want
steps.text: If you inserted the wrong style or picked the wrong cells, press Command-Z to undo. Press Shift-Command-Z to redo the change if you change your mind.
steps.tip: Undo is the fastest way back if the chart plots the wrong data.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that the values are numbers, not text. Select the labels and the numbers together, then click the Chart button again.

troubleshooting.problem: A row is missing from the chart
troubleshooting.fix: Hidden and filtered data is excluded by default. Click the chart, open the Format sidebar, click the Chart tab, and select Hidden Data in Chart Options.

troubleshooting.problem: Only some groups show up in the chart
troubleshooting.fix: Collapsed groups plot only their visible data. Expand the groups, then select the cells again.

troubleshooting.problem: The chart shows a Large Data Set message
troubleshooting.fix: Numbers shows a sample for large column, bar, line, or area charts. Your table data is unchanged, so the sample only affects the drawing.

troubleshooting.problem: The series run the wrong way
troubleshooting.fix: Click the chart, click Edit Data References, change the series orientation in the bottom bar pop-up, then click Done.

troubleshooting.problem: The chart looks flat in Numbers for iCloud
troubleshooting.fix: Imported 3D charts show as 2D on the web but keep their 3D data. Open the file in Numbers on Mac, iPhone, or iPad to see them in 3D.
